root_cause_analysis: An external drift event with severity 0.1846 was detected on the jitter component. Recent network telemetry indicates moderate radio load (PRB utilization at 52.66%) and stable mobility (UE speed at 4.10 m/s), but environmental shift has caused parameter staleness in the existing jitter estimation model.
decision_rationale: The jitter component is an existing part of the digital twin scope and has no previous adaptation attempts on record. Since the issue stems from environmental parameter drift rather than an omitted network phenomenon or structural model invalidation, retraining the existing model pipeline on recent data via recalibration is the optimal adaptation choice.
verification_explanation: The candidate model for the 'jitter' component was rejected by the deterministic acceptance gate because it failed the critical fidelity improvement check (fidelity_improved). To be accepted, the candidate model required a fidelity score greater than 19.9188 (the baseline plus a verification delta of 0.01). The recalibration attempt in response to external drift on 'jitter' (severity 0.185) produced a model with significantly worse performance than the active production baseline.
